chunks: Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us. He said: I heard a man from our companions say:

When Harun al-Rashid imprisoned Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon him), night befell him. He feared that Harun would kill him. So Musa renewed his purification, faced the qibla, prayed four units for Allah the Mighty and Majestic, then supplicated: O my Master, save me from the prison of Harun and deliver me from his hands. O deliverer of the tree from between sand, clay, and water; O deliverer of milk from between excretion and blood; O deliverer of the child from between the placenta and the womb; O deliverer of fire from between iron and stone; O deliverer of the spirit from between the intestines and the bowels — deliver me from the hands of Harun.

He said: When Musa (peace be upon him) supplicated with these supplications, Harun saw a black man in his dream, with a sword unsheathed in his hand, standing over Harun's head, saying: O Harun, release Musa b. Ja'far, or else I will strike your head with this sword. Harun feared his awe and called for his gatekeeper. He said: Go to the prison and release Musa b. Ja'far. The gatekeeper knocked on the prison door. The warden asked: Who is this? He said: The caliph calls for Musa b. Ja'far. The jailer shouted: O Musa, the caliph calls you. Musa stood terrified, saying: He calls me only for evil. He came to Harun trembling. He said: Peace upon Harun. Harun returned the greeting then said: I adjure you by Allah, did you supplicate tonight? He said: Yes. Harun said: What were they? He described his supplication. Harun said: Allah has answered your supplication.

O gatekeeper, release this one. Then he called for robes and bestowed three upon him, mounted him on his horse, honoured him, and made him a companion for himself. Then he said: Give me the words so I may memorize them. Then he called for an inkwell and paper and wrote these words. He said: So he released him and handed him to his gatekeeper to deliver him to the house. So Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon them both) became honoured and noble with Harun, and he would visit him every Thursday.

key_terms.القبلة: Qibla — the direction of the Ka'ba in Mecca, toward which Muslims pray
key_terms.خلع: Khila' — honorary robes bestowed as a mark of distinction
key_terms.مخلص: Deliverer — one who extracts/delivers, repeated five times addressing God
key_terms.نديم: Nadim — a boon companion or court companion
key_terms.هارون الرشيد: Harun al-Rashid — the fifth Abbasid caliph (r. 786-809 CE) who imprisoned Imam al-Kadhim

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam Musa al-Kadhim make in prison that led Harun al-Rashid to free him?
ai.summary: An unnamed companion narrates the dramatic story of Imam Musa al-Kadhim's imprisonment by Harun al-Rashid. Fearing for his life at night, the Imam performed four units of prayer and made a beautiful supplication calling upon God as the One who delivers the tree from sand, milk from blood, children from the womb, fire from stone, and spirits from the body. In response, Harun saw a threatening dream-figure commanding the Imam's release, leading him not only to free the Imam but to honour him with robes, a horse, and regular audiences every Thursday.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us. He said: I heard a man from our companions say:

When Harun al-Rashid imprisoned Musa b. Ja`far (as), night befell him. He feared that Harun may kill him. So, Musa (as) renewed this purification, faced the qibla, prayed four voluntary units for Allah, then supplicated with this supplication: O my Master! Save me from the prison of Harun, and deliver me from his hands, O deliverer of the tree from the sand, clay, and water; O deliverer of milk from excretion and blood; O deliverer of the child from the placenta and the womb; O deliverer of fire from iron and stone; O deliverer of spirit from the intestines, deliver me from the hands of Harun.

He said: When Musa (as) supplicated with this supplication, Harun saw a black man in his dream. In his hand was a sword as he stood over the head of Harun, as he was saying: “O Harun! Let Musa b. Ja`far go. If you don’t, then I will strike your neck with this sword.” So, Harun feared his awesome aura, and he called for his gatekeeper. When the gatekeeper came, he said to him: Go to the prison and free Musa b. Ja`far. So, the gatekeeper went to the gate of the prison and knocked on it. The warden answered him and said: Who is this? He said: Surely, the caliph is calling for Musa b. Ja`far, so free him from your prison. So, the warden yelled: O Musa! The caliph calls for you. So, Musa (as) stood suddenly, surprised and saying: He does not call for me tonight except to do an evil thing to me. So, he stood weeping, grieving, worried, and sorrowful about his life. He was taken to Harun shaking, so he said: Peace be to Harun (salam `ala harun). So, he responded, then Harun said to him: I adjure you by Allah, did you make any supplication in the middle of this night? So, he said: Yes. He said: What was it? He said: I renewed my purification, and I prayed four voluntary prayers for Allah, and I raised my sight to the sky, and I said: “O my Master! Deliver me from the hands of Harun and his evil”, and he mentioned what was left of his supplication. So, Harun said: Allah has answered your supplication. O gatekeeper, free him.

Then, he called for a robe, and he put three robes onto him, and mounted him on his horse, and honoured him, and regretfully sent him off. Then, he said: Give me the words [to the supplication] so that I may memorize it. Then, he called for a tablet and wrote the words. He said: So, he sent him away, and he surrendered him to his gatekeeper so that he could send him to the house. So, Musa b. Ja`far (as) became honoured by Harun, and he would visit him every Thursday.
